```{python}
#| label: setup
import sys
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import HTML, Markdown

ROOT = Path.cwd()
while not (ROOT / "_quarto.yml").exists():
    ROOT = ROOT.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
import chart_style as cs

d = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data/processed/core_daily.csv", parse_dates=["date"]).set_index("date")
m = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data/processed/core_monthly.csv")
m["month"] = pd.to_datetime(m["month"])
m = m.set_index("month")
events = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data/events.csv")

d = d[d["hours_with_price"] >= 20]            # skip days with too few published hours
VOL_FROM = pd.Timestamp("2017-12-01")           # GÖP and bilateral volumes are published from here
for df in (d, m):
    df.loc[df.index < VOL_FROM, ["gop_mwh", "bilateral_mwh"]] = float("nan")
last = d.index.max()
import price_limits as pl
d["cap"] = pl.cap_on(d.index).to_numpy()      # lira cap in force that day (empty before 1 April 2022)
# Euro and dollar cap = lira cap divided by the exchange rate implied by that day's PTF in each currency
d["cap_eur"] = d["cap"] / (d["ptf_mean"] / d["ptf_eur_mean"].where(d["ptf_eur_mean"] > 0))
d["cap_usd"] = d["cap"] / (d["ptf_mean"] / d["ptf_usd_mean"].where(d["ptf_usd_mean"] > 0))
fmt = lambda v, dec=0: "–" if pd.isna(v) else f"{v:,.{dec}f}"
```

```{python}
#| label: tiles
def window(days, end=last):
    return d.loc[end - pd.Timedelta(days=days - 1): end]

w30 = window(30)
w30_ly = window(30, last - pd.DateOffset(years=1))
ytd = d.loc[f"{last.year}-01-01": last]
chg = (w30["ptf_eur_mean"].mean() / w30_ly["ptf_eur_mean"].mean() - 1) * 100

tiles = [
    (f"PTF on {last:%d %b %Y}", f"{fmt(d.loc[last, 'ptf_mean'])} TL/MWh",
     f"{fmt(d.loc[last, 'ptf_eur_mean'], 1)} EUR/MWh · SMF {fmt(d.loc[last, 'smf_mean'])} TL/MWh"),
    ("PTF, last 30 days", f"{fmt(w30['ptf_mean'].mean())} TL/MWh",
     f"{fmt(w30['ptf_eur_mean'].mean(), 1)} EUR/MWh · {chg:+.0f}% in EUR vs a year earlier".replace("-", "−")),
    (f"PTF, {last.year} so far", f"{fmt(ytd['ptf_mean'].mean())} TL/MWh",
     f"{fmt(ytd['ptf_eur_mean'].mean(), 1)} EUR/MWh · simple average of daily means"),
]
HTML('<div class="tile-grid">' + "".join(
    f'<div class="tile"><p class="eyebrow">{a}</p><h3>{b}</h3><p>{c}</p></div>' for a, b, c in tiles) + "</div>")
```

## Daily, weekly and monthly prices

PTF is the hourly price set in the day-ahead market (GÖP). AOF is the volume-weighted average price of trades in the intraday market (GİP), from July 2015. SMF is the price of the last balancing instruction the system operator used in each hour (DGP). All three are averages of hourly prices in Turkish lira. The dashed line is the price cap in force (the average cap in the period for weekly and monthly views); it starts on 1 April 2022, and the [price limits](#price-limits-a-cap-and-a-floor) section below explains it. Use the buttons to change the time step and the range; click a name in the legend to hide or show a line.

```{python}
#| label: price-chart
import plotly.graph_objects as go

cols3 = ["ptf_mean", "smf_mean", "aof_mean"]
cols4 = cols3 + ["cap"]
weekly = d[cols4].resample("W-MON", label="left", closed="left").mean()
monthly = d[cols4].resample("MS").mean().reindex(m.index)   # the average cap in force in the month
monthly[cols3] = m[cols3]
views = {"Daily": d[cols4], "Weekly": weekly, "Monthly": monthly}

fig = cs.figure(None, "TL/MWh", height=460)
for i, (name, df) in enumerate(views.items()):
    for key, col in (("ptf", "ptf_mean"), ("smf", "smf_mean"), ("aof", "aof_mean")):
        cs.add_line(fig, df.index, df[col], "prices", key, unit=" TL/MWh", end_label=False)
        fig.data[-1].update(visible=(name == "Weekly"), legendgroup=key, showlegend=(name == "Weekly"))
    cs.add_cap_line(fig, df.index, df["cap"], unit=" TL/MWh")
    fig.data[-1].update(visible=(name == "Weekly"), legendgroup="cap", showlegend=(name == "Weekly"))

n = len(fig.data)
buttons = []
for i, name in enumerate(views):
    vis = [j // 4 == i for j in range(n)]
    buttons.append(dict(label=name, method="update", args=[{"visible": vis, "showlegend": vis}]))
fig.update_layout(
    updatemenus=[dict(type="buttons", direction="right", buttons=buttons, active=1, x=0, y=1.04,
                      xanchor="left", yanchor="bottom", showactive=True, pad=dict(r=6, t=0),
                      font=dict(size=12))],
    margin=dict(t=40),
)
fig.update_xaxes(
    range=[last - pd.DateOffset(years=2), last],
    rangeselector=dict(buttons=[dict(count=3, label="3M", step="month", stepmode="backward"),
                                dict(count=1, label="1Y", step="year", stepmode="backward"),
                                dict(count=5, label="5Y", step="year", stepmode="backward"),
                                dict(step="all", label="All")],
                       x=1, xanchor="right", y=1.04, yanchor="bottom", font=dict(size=12)),
)
cs.add_events(fig, events, "ptf")
cs.style_controls(fig)
cs.show(fig)
```

## The long view in euros

Lira prices rose more than twentyfold between 2011 and 2026, mostly because of inflation and the weaker lira, so a long lira series hides real changes. EPİAŞ also publishes every hourly PTF in euros and US dollars, converted at that day's exchange rate. The chart shows weekly averages in either currency. The dashed line is the price cap in that currency: the lira cap divided by the exchange rate implied by each day's PTF, so it moves with the exchange rate even when the lira cap is unchanged. It starts on 1 April 2022, when the cap became a fixed amount; before that it followed a formula. Switch to **Log** to compare changes in percentage terms: on a log scale a doubling looks the same in 2013 and in 2022, so quieter years are no longer flattened by the 2022 gas crisis.

```{python}
#| label: long-chart

wkc = wkc.mean().where(wkc.count() >= 5)

for name, (col, unit) in cur.items():

fig2.update_layout(

        dict(type="buttons", direction="right", active=0, x=0, y=1.03, xanchor="left", yanchor="bottom",
             buttons=[dict(label=k, method="update",
                           args=[{"visible": [(j % len(cur)) == i for j in range(2 * len(cur))]},

fig2.update_xaxes(rangeselector=dict(buttons=[dict(count=2, label="2Y", step="year", stepmode="backward"),
                                              dict(count=5, label="5Y", step="year", stepmode="backward"),
                                              dict(step="all", label="All")],
                                     x=1, xanchor="right", y=1.03, yanchor="bottom"))
```

## Yearly averages

```{python}
#| label: yearly-table
y = m.copy()
y["year"] = y.index.year
h = y["hours_with_price"]
agg = pd.DataFrame({
    "PTF (TL/MWh)": (y["ptf_mean"] * h).groupby(y["year"]).sum() / h.groupby(y["year"]).sum(),
    "PTF (EUR/MWh)": (y["ptf_eur_mean"] * h).groupby(y["year"]).sum() / h.where(y["ptf_eur_mean"].notna()).groupby(y["year"]).sum(),
    "PTF (USD/MWh)": (y["ptf_usd_mean"] * h).groupby(y["year"]).sum() / h.where(y["ptf_usd_mean"].notna()).groupby(y["year"]).sum(),
    "SMF (TL/MWh)": (y["smf_mean"] * h).groupby(y["year"]).sum() / h.where(y["smf_mean"].notna()).groupby(y["year"]).sum(),
    "AOF (TL/MWh)": (y["aof_mean"] * h).groupby(y["year"]).sum() / h.where(y["aof_mean"].notna()).groupby(y["year"]).sum(),
    "Hours system short": (y["deficit_share"] * h).groupby(y["year"]).sum() / h.where(y["deficit_share"].notna()).groupby(y["year"]).sum(),
})
agg = agg.sort_index(ascending=False)
partial = {agg.index.max(): f"{agg.index.max()} (to {last:%d %b})", agg.index.min(): f"{agg.index.min()} (from Nov)"}
agg.index = [partial.get(i, str(i)) for i in agg.index]
out = agg.copy()
for c in ["PTF (TL/MWh)", "SMF (TL/MWh)", "AOF (TL/MWh)"]:
    out[c] = agg[c].map(lambda v: fmt(v))
for c in ["PTF (EUR/MWh)", "PTF (USD/MWh)"]:
    out[c] = agg[c].map(lambda v: fmt(v, 1))
out["Hours system short"] = agg["Hours system short"].map(lambda v: "–" if pd.isna(v) else f"{v:.0%}")
Markdown(out.to_markdown(disable_numparse=True, colalign=["left"] + ["right"] * len(out.columns)))
```

Yearly figures are simple averages of hourly prices: every hour counts the same. SMF starts in April 2014 on the transparency platform, AOF in July 2015 when the intraday market opened. "Hours system short" is the share of hours in which the system needed extra energy (Enerji Açığı), so balancing instructions were mostly to increase output.

Prices are averages of EPİAŞ hourly data, in Turkish lira, euros or US dollars per MWh; shares are fractions of hours (0.65 = 65%). ## Where electricity is traded

Electricity changes hands in three places: bilateral contracts (İA) agreed directly between companies, the day-ahead market (GÖP) run by EPİAŞ, and the intraday market (GİP), where positions are adjusted up to shortly before delivery. Bilateral volume counts every contract, including resales between traders, so traded volume is larger than consumption. Volumes are published from December 2017.

```{python}
#| label: market-chart
mk = m.loc[VOL_FROM:, ["bilateral_mwh", "gop_mwh", "idm_mwh", "consumption_mwh", "hours_with_price"]]

keys = [("bilateral", "bilateral_mwh"), ("gop", "gop_mwh"), ("gip", "idm_mwh")]
figm = cs.figure(None, "TWh per month", height=440)
for key, col in keys:
    cs.add_area(figm, mk.index, mk[col] / 1e6, "markets", key, unit=" TWh", hover_fmt=",.1f")
twh_hover = [t.hovertemplate for t in figm.data]

figm.update_layout(
    margin=dict(t=48), legend=dict(traceorder="reversed"),
    updatemenus=[dict(type="buttons", direction="right", active=0, x=0, y=1.03, xanchor="left", yanchor="bottom",
                      buttons=[dict(label="TWh", method="update",
                                    args=[{"groupnorm": [""] * 3, "hovertemplate": twh_hover},

cs.style_controls(figm)
cs.show(figm)
```

The day-ahead market is where the reference price is set, but most electricity is sold through bilateral contracts. The intraday market is small: a few percent of traded volume, used to correct positions as forecasts change.

## Price limits: a cap and a floor

Offers and prices in the day-ahead market must stay between a minimum and a maximum set by the regulator, EPDK. The minimum has always been zero. The maximum has changed many times; the balancing market (SMF) works under the same limits. Both are published in the Official Gazette.

**Why a cap?** The decisions we read state the limit but not the reasoning, so this part is our reading of press reports and of the market's structure. A cap limits what one hour can cost buyers when supply is tight, when a few large plants set the price, or when gas costs jump with the exchange rate. Until spring 2022 the cap followed a formula: three times the trailing twelve-month weighted average PTF, and at most 2,000 TL/MWh, so it rose as prices rose. Since 1 April 2022 it is a fixed amount in lira that the board changes by decision.

**Why a floor at zero?** Bids below zero are not accepted, so the price cannot go negative. Most European day-ahead markets allow negative prices, down to −500 EUR/MWh in the coupled EU market. In Türkiye the decisions simply state a minimum of 0. When must-run and renewable output exceeds demand, the price sits at zero, so zero-price hours show that there is a surplus but not how large it is.

**What the limits do to the data.** At the cap or the floor the price stops carrying information about scarcity or surplus: it is cut off, not observed. Averages, spreads and volatility measures are therefore likely to be smaller than they would be without limits, and a cap that is hit as often as this one (see below) shapes the whole price distribution.

```{python}
#| label: limits-data
import plotly.graph_objects as go

caps = pl.load_caps()
CAP_FROM = caps["effective_date"].min()

dd_ = d.loc[CAP_FROM:].copy()
dd_["cap_day"] = (dd_["ptf_max"] >= dd_["cap"] - pl.TOLERANCE).astype(float)    # at least one hour at the cap

mm = m.loc[CAP_FROM:].copy()
mm = mm[mm["hours_with_price"] >= mm.index.days_in_month * 24 - 1]                # full months only
mm["cap_days"] = dd_["cap_day"].resample("MS").sum().reindex(mm.index)
HAS_HOURS = "ptf_cap_hours" in m.columns and m["ptf_cap_hours"].notna().any()
if HAS_HOURS:
    mm["cap_hours"] = m["ptf_cap_hours"].reindex(mm.index)

cap_now, cap_start = dd_["cap"].iloc[-1], caps["max_tl_mwh"].iloc[0]
eur_peak_day = dd_["cap_eur"].idxmax()
y1 = dd_.loc[last - pd.DateOffset(years=1) + pd.Timedelta(days=1): last]
share_days = y1["cap_day"].mean()
if HAS_HOURS:
    m12 = m.iloc[-12:]
    cap_h, all_h = m12["ptf_cap_hours"].sum(), m12["hours_with_price"].sum()
    hours_txt = (f" Counted by the hour, PTF was at the cap in **{cap_h / all_h:.1%} of all hours** "
                 f"({cap_h:,.0f} of {all_h:,.0f}) over the last 12 calendar months, counting the current month so far.")
else:
    hours_txt = ""
Markdown(
    f"In the last 12 months, PTF reached the cap in at least one hour on **{share_days:.0%} of days** "
    f"({int(y1['cap_day'].sum())} of {len(y1)}).{hours_txt} "
    f"The cap is now {cap_now:,.0f} TL/MWh, about {dd_['cap_eur'].iloc[-30:].mean():,.0f} EUR/MWh at today's rate. "
    f"At its highest in euros ({eur_peak_day:%b %Y}) it was about {dd_.loc[eur_peak_day, 'cap_eur']:,.0f} EUR/MWh: "
    f"lira cap increases have not kept pace with the lira's fall, so the cap has become tighter in real terms."
)
```

### How often prices sit on the limits

```{python}
               hover_fmt=",.0f", unit=" hours")

cs.show(figc)
```

```{python}
#| label: cap-table
rows = caps.copy()
rows["Effective"] = rows["effective_date"].dt.strftime("%d %b %Y")
rows["Cap (TL/MWh)"] = rows["max_tl_mwh"].map(lambda v: f"{v:,.0f}")
rows["Status"] = rows["status"].map({"verified": "Verified", "draft": "Seen in data, decision not confirmed"})
rows["Source"] = rows["source"].apply(lambda u: f"[link]({u})" if isinstance(u, str) and u.startswith("http") else "–")
tab = rows[["Effective", "Cap (TL/MWh)", "Status", "Source"]].iloc[::-1].reset_index(drop=True)
Markdown(tab.to_markdown(index=False, disable_numparse=True, colalign=["left", "right", "left", "left"]))
```

*Verified* means a dated press report of the decision (or the Official Gazette notice it quotes) agrees with the data. *Seen in data* means the limit shows up as a price ceiling in the data on that date, but we have not yet confirmed the decision or its date; we mark those until we do. Effective dates are the first delivery day at the new limit and can differ from the decision date by a few days.

```{python}
#| label: limits-yearly
yr = dd_.groupby(dd_.index.year)
cols = {"Cap at year end (TL/MWh)": yr["cap"].last().map(lambda v: f"{v:,.0f}"),
        "Days with a cap hour": yr["cap_day"].sum().map(lambda v: f"{v:,.0f}"),
        "Share of days": yr["cap_day"].mean().map(lambda v: f"{v:.0%}")}
if HAS_HOURS:
    ch = m.loc[CAP_FROM:, "ptf_cap_hours"].groupby(m.loc[CAP_FROM:].index.year).sum(min_count=1)
    zh = m.loc[CAP_FROM:, "ptf_zero_hours"].groupby(m.loc[CAP_FROM:].index.year).sum(min_count=1)
    hh = m.loc[CAP_FROM:, "hours_with_price"].groupby(m.loc[CAP_FROM:].index.year).sum(min_count=1)
    cols["Hours at the cap"] = ch.map(lambda v: f"{v:,.0f}")
    cols["Share of hours"] = (ch / hh).map(lambda v: f"{v:.1%}")
    cols["Hours at zero"] = zh.map(lambda v: f"{v:,.0f}")
yt = pd.DataFrame(cols).sort_index(ascending=False)
yt.index = [f"{y} (to {last:%d %b})" if y == last.year else (f"{y} (from 1 Apr)" if y == CAP_FROM.year else str(y)) for y in yt.index]
Markdown(yt.to_markdown(disable_numparse=True, colalign=["left"] + ["right"] * len(yt.columns)))
```

Before 1 April 2022 the cap was formula-based, so the fixed-cap table above does not reach back further. The monthly maximum prices of July 2021 to March 2022 rise in steps (617, 636, 674, 718 and then 1,078 to 1,745 TL/MWh) and equal the daily maximum on most days, which fits a cap that was rebuilt each month; we have not verified the formula's start date, so hours at the cap are not counted for that period.

### Hours at the cap, month by month

```{python}
#| label: limits-monthly-tables
if HAS_HOURS:
    mo = m.loc[CAP_FROM:, ["ptf_cap_hours", "hours_with_price"]].copy()
    partial = mo["hours_with_price"] < mo.index.days_in_month * 24 - 1
    mo["share"] = mo["ptf_cap_hours"] / mo["hours_with_price"]
    mo["year"], mo["mon"] = mo.index.year, mo.index.month
    names = ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"]

    def grid(value, fmt_, total):
        g = mo.pivot(index="year", columns="mon", values=value).reindex(columns=range(1, 13))
        out = g.copy().astype(object)
        for (r, c), v in g.stack(future_stack=True).items():
            txt = "–" if pd.isna(v) else fmt_(v)
            if not pd.isna(v) and partial.get(pd.Timestamp(year=r, month=c, day=1), False):
                txt += "*"
            out.loc[r, c] = txt
        out.columns = names
        out["Total"] = total.map(lambda v: fmt_(v)).reindex(out.index)
        out.index.name = "Year"
        return out.sort_index(ascending=False)

    tot_h = mo.groupby("year")["ptf_cap_hours"].sum()
    tot_s = mo.groupby("year")["ptf_cap_hours"].sum() / mo.groupby("year")["hours_with_price"].sum()
    g1 = grid("ptf_cap_hours", lambda v: f"{v:,.0f}", tot_h)
    g2 = grid("share", lambda v: f"{v:.0%}", tot_s)
    ca = ["left"] + ["right"] * 13
    txt_ = ("**Number of hours at the cap**\n\n"
            + g1.to_markdown(disable_numparse=True, colalign=ca)
            + "\n\n**Share of the month's hours at the cap**\n\n"
            + g2.to_markdown(disable_numparse=True, colalign=ca)
            + "\n\nA star marks a month still in progress. 2022 starts in April, when the cap became a fixed amount, so its yearly figure covers April to December.")
else:
    txt_ = "Monthly hour counts appear after the next data refresh."
Markdown(txt_)
```

```{python}
#| label: limits-downloads
stamp = f"{last:%Y%m%d}"
cap_out = caps[["decision_date", "effective_date", "max_tl_mwh", "min_tl_mwh", "status", "source", "note"]].copy()
cap_out["effective_date"] = cap_out["effective_date"].dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
lim = mm[["cap_days"] + (["cap_hours"] if HAS_HOURS else []) + ["ptf_zero_hours"]].rename(
    columns={"cap_days": "days_with_hour_at_cap", "cap_hours": "hours_at_cap", "ptf_zero_hours": "hours_at_zero"})
if HAS_HOURS:
    lim["share_of_hours_at_cap"] = (mm["cap_hours"] / mm["hours_with_price"]).round(4)
lim.index = lim.index.strftime("%Y-%m")
HTML(
    cs.download_link(cap_out, f"trpowerlab_ptf_price_caps_{stamp}.csv", "Cap history (CSV)")
    + cs.download_link(lim.rename_axis("month").reset_index(), f"trpowerlab_ptf_limit_hours_monthly_{stamp}.csv", "Monthly hours at the limits (CSV)")
)
```

## Notes

- **Source:** EPİAŞ Şeffaflık Platformu, through the open source [eptr2](https://github.com/Tideseed/eptr2) package. Data to `{python} f"{last:%d %B %Y}"`.
- **Price caps:** PTF and SMF are limited to a range set by EPDK. The cap changed many times since April 2022 and PTF reaches it on many days; see the section above.
- **Gaps:** a few hours on old daylight saving days are missing in the source data and are left out, not filled.
- See the [methodology](../../methodology.qmd) for definitions and the data quality notes.
